chapter: Sid Leprotti and the So Different band
title: Looking for Wade Whaley; digression; 1918 draft and France
summary: Searching for Wade Whaley, a muddled aside about a drummer and band picture, then his move from LA and 1918 draft.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: You know, we tried to find out where Wade Whaley was. And nobody down there knew Paul Howard thought he was up this way. Maybe he said try San Jose.

Yeah, when he left here he went to San Jose. And the next time I heard he went to San Diego. Because I was down in Los Angeles. I was told that he had a little cigar stand and whatnot. And I went all up and down Central Avenue. And nobody knew nothing about him.
We couldn't find any trace of him there. No. Orie the other night when we talked to Orie on the phone said that he thought he, I believe he said he'd seen him in San Diego and he played down there.

I think you're wrong. You might have seen him down there. Just a little small town. He's not far from here. Might be around. But I've been looking at him. You know your friend, the drummer that comes to see you all the time. The trumpet player, them two boys that just play in your band. Yeah. How long did you live down in Los Angeles then? From 1915, you say you moved out about.
Yes. And then, let's see, in 1918, I was drafted in World War I. Went to France, and when I come back is when I started working with Sid. And I left. After that? Yes.
